apps.releaseNotes:
# Clint Gecko v1.0.0

## Introducing Clint Gecko!

Clint Browser is getting a new sibling! Unlike the original Clint Browser, which runs on Android System WebView, Clint Gecko is powered by Firefox's GeckoView engine.

And because of that, Clint Gecko brings extension support and background playback to the Clint experience!

But that's not all. Since Clint Gecko is an official fork of Clint Browser, with the browser engine being the main change, it also retains the built-in ADM (Advanced Download Manager) and Media Capture features, making it easier to download files and capture online media directly from your browser.

---

## Key Features

- Firefox-based browsing with GeckoView
- Browser extension support (thanks to @brnwlshubh for suggesting this [#18](https://github.com/jhaiian/ClintBrowser/issues/18))
- Background playback
- Built-in Advanced Download Manager (ADM)
- Built-in Media Capture

---

Clint is no longer limited to one browser engine. You can stick with the original WebView-based Clint Browser or choose Clint Gecko for a Firefox-powered experience with extension support.

And don't worry! The original Clint Browser will continue to be maintained as the lighter version, so you can choose whichever browser suits your needs best.

**Two engines. One Clint.**

---

apps.releaseNotes:
Infinite scrolling of the home pages, a way to close the set-as-default card, and page dots that show on light wallpapers. Updating keeps your layout, widgets and settings.

**Added**
- **Infinite scrolling.** Swiping on from the last home page brings the first one back, and swiping back from the first page brings the last, following your finger, requested in #5. It is on by default; turn it off under Settings ▸ Home screen ▸ Infinite scrolling. Dragging icons and widgets is unchanged: a drag never wraps, and holding an icon at the right edge still opens a new empty page. If you have chosen a Left edge app, the swipe right on the first page keeps opening it, so the first page then wraps only forwards.
- **"Not now" on the set-as-default card.** The card that asks you to make ARK-launcher your default home app can now be closed, requested in #6. It stays closed on this phone, and Settings still has the "Set as default launcher" row.

**Changed**
- **The ends of the pages.** With infinite scrolling off, or with a single page, a swipe past the last page no longer slides onto an empty page that then slides back (#7). Both ends now stop with Android's edge stretch and say "No more pages". The empty page past the last one is only for dropping icons.
- **Page dots on light wallpapers.** The dots and the home-page marker have a soft dark shadow, so they no longer vanish on a light wallpaper.
- **TalkBack and Switch Access.** Paging at either end does what a swipe does: it wraps when infinite scrolling is on, and otherwise stops and says "No more pages".

No new permissions. Get updates from this page, from [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium) with this repository as the source, from [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/org.arkikeskus.launcher/), or from the app store you use.

apps.description: Free, encrypted internet calls between friends, inside a complete replacement for your phone's Phone and Messages apps. Android, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material 3; no ads, no tracking.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's new

**ARK internet calls are now in the public release.** Create an ARK code in Settings, share it, link a friend's code on their contact card, and calls between you go over the internet — free, end-to-end encrypted (WebRTC with DTLS-SRTP), phone to phone. When the other phone cannot be reached the very same call goes over your carrier, so a call always goes through. An incoming ARK call rings on a locked, sleeping phone. Until you create a code the app makes no network connection at all; see the README for what the signaling server sees.

**Nine new languages:** Swedish, German, French, Spanish, Estonian, Russian, Portuguese, Italian and Polish, alongside English and Finnish. The app follows the device language; Android 13 and newer can pick a language per app.

**Backup to a file.** Settings → Backup saves your settings, blocking rules, speed dials, your ARK code with its linked contacts and the WhatsApp call history into one file, password-protected by default, and restores it on the same or another phone. Before anything is replaced, the restore shows which ARK code and how many linked contacts the file brings. Calls, messages and contacts are not included; they stay in Android's own backup.

**Do Not Disturb now treats an ARK call from a starred contact like a carrier call** from that contact: the incoming-call notification names the caller, so the "calls from contacts" exceptions match it.

The README has been rewritten and the step-by-step instructions moved to a [user guide](https://github.com/jrs8205/ARK-phone/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md).

Update from 1.27 in place; the APK carries the same signature and your data is kept. Requires Android 8.0 or newer.

apps.description: Android app store for open-source apps on GitHub. Developers publish an app by adding the topic "arkstore" to its repository; the store installs and updates APKs straight from GitHub releases.
apps.releaseNotes:
- **Back up the installed apps**: in the settings, under App backup, the apps installed from outside Google Play are saved as their APK files, with the splits of a bundle, to a folder on the device, on a card or in a cloud service the file picker shows, or to one zip file for moving to another phone or to a service such as Google Drive. A folder stays up to date and copies only what has changed; a zip is written whole each time. The list of apps has the whole page, with a search and the choices all, none or only the apps not from Play. The store's own settings go along
- **Restore** from such a folder or zip file, on this or another device: the page tells of each app whether it is missing, behind, the same, newer, signed with another key or in need of a newer Android, and installs what is chosen one after the other. The sources, bookmarks and settings in the backup can be brought back at the same time
- **Recent backups and restores** in the settings: when, to or from where, how many apps of what size, and how each went
- **Root**: on a rooted device (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch) root can be turned on in the settings. Installs, updates, removals and restores then go through without Android asking. Root is asked for when it is first needed; if it is refused or missing, the usual prompts are used and the settings say so
- **App data in the backup**: with root on, a backup can include the apps' own data, encrypted with a password if one is given. A restore puts the data back only into the app it was taken from, signed with the same key, and only whole: every part is checked before any is put in place, and the old data is kept until all are. Without root, the apps' own data is not part of the backup, since Android does not let a store read it
- **The settings as a page of their own**, with the way back at the top, instead of a sheet pulled up over the list

Download `ARK-Store-1.9.0.apk` below and open it on your phone to install, or update from inside ARK-Store.

apps.description: Android device monitor with a home-screen widget, per-app usage insights and a charging screensaver. Fully offline - no internet permission. GPL-3.0-or-later.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's changed

- **Privacy log (extended access).** The Apps tab has a PRIVACY band; *Open* shows Android's own record of which apps used the camera, the microphone and the location: when, for how long, from the background or not, app by app and moment by moment. On Android 17, which keeps them, refused requests show too. Shown, never stored; without extended access the band offers Android's own Privacy dashboard instead.
- **System apps page (extended access).** The Apps tab's SYSTEM APPS band leads to every app on the system image, with a search. *Remove* takes a preinstalled app you do not use away from this user only (`pm uninstall --user`); the system image's copy stays and *Restore* brings it back. Every removal is asked about first, the apps the phone depends on say what breaks and want that acknowledged, and the ones it cannot do without (Android's core, the home screen, keyboard, phone app and web view in use, Device Watch itself) cannot be removed from here. The verdict is read again just before the command, and a removal or restore the shell calls done but the package manager contradicts is reported as nothing changed.
- **Kernel page (root): sleep.** The kernel's sleep attempts, what stopped the last one, and the wakeup sources that woke the phone most or held it awake longest.
- **The app no longer appears in its own log.** Every location-flavoured read (cell list, Wi-Fi name and details, service state) now happens only while the app is on screen and goes through one gate, so Device Watch's service no longer leaves refusals in Android's privacy log by the minute.
- **Wi-Fi under a VPN.** The Wi-Fi band, signal, speed, standard and security come from the Wi-Fi network's own capabilities, so a VPN no longer hides or mislabels them; the name is read again when the network changes within the minute.
- **Android 17.** The battery's design capacity from the kernel where Android hides the power profile (through extended access where the phone keeps the file from apps), and whether developer options and USB debugging are on, read through extended access since Android 17 hides the switches.

More in the [FAQ](https://github.com/jrs8205/Device-Watch/blob/main/FAQ.md) and the [privacy policy](https://github.com/jrs8205/Device-Watch/blob/main/PRIVACY.md).

## Installing

Updates cleanly over v1.4.x and later. If you are coming from v1.3.1 or older (package `com.example.modernwidget`), uninstall the old app first — it is a different package and will not update.

**APK SHA-256:** `00d9edfc14a7464e557a417c8ca22429e6c930ae652a5fe5b4cb16000fea86c2`
**Signing cert SHA-256:** `a787d3be1fa4d58751e246dba9b8f1ded5b6a00ab2675367bf49420928e1a51a`

- **Kolme kieltä.** Sovellus seuraa puhelimen kieltä: suomi ja ruotsi omalla kielellään, kaikki muut kielet englanniksi. Kielen voi vaihtaa sovelluskohtaisesti Androidin asetuksista. Nimi on Sää & Sähkö, Väder & Börsel tai Weather & Spot Prices.
